questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Compliance and Auditability?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Auditability depends on recorded approvals, workflow run history, source-to-artifact traceability, scoped credentials, and reviewable policy changes.
questions.answer_key: Auditability depends on recorded approvals, workflow run history, source-to-artifact traceability, scoped credentials, and reviewable policy changes.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of compliance and auditability: Auditability depends on recorded approvals, workflow run history, source-to-artifact traceability, scoped credentials, and reviewable policy changes. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.

questions.answer_key: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to compliance and auditability?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Auditability depends on recorded approvals, workflow run history, source-to-artifact traceability, scoped credentials, and reviewable policy changes. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
